turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I heard that you've been having, uh, some difficulty breathing and you've been coughing. Can you tell a little, tell me a little bit more about that.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so uh a couple of days ago. I just started to not feel so well and I've been having this cough and trouble breathing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, have you ever had anything like this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do have a, uh, cough regularly, but I mean, I, I think that's related to maybe smoking. It's something that was going on for a few years. This coughs a little bit different.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, in what way is this different?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's been happening more often throughout the day and. And bringing up more more mucus, it seems like.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and then you said it start started a couple days ago, is that correct?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I think like Monday, so, uh, yeah I guess like 3 days ago then.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and since you noticed it has it gotten worse over those three days.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I would say uh today's the worst day I've continually felt um sick.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And how frequently are you coughing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh I would say maybe a couple of times per hour. I'm I'm filling up a some tissues with sputum.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And what does that? What does that sputum look like?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's like a dark greenish yellow colour.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, um and. Is there anything that you've changed recently in your life or any kind of things that have provoked your cough that you know of?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Ugh, no, I can't think of anything. I've been kind of sticking to my regular routines.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and is there anything that makes, uh, makes it worse, say any position or anything that you do in your day to day routine you find makes you cough more?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um And not really I can't. I can't think of anything.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, have you taken any any medicine or anything to try to help with us?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um. No, I I've I I do have a little bit of pain so I was. I did take some Tylenol and some Advil over the last few days, but that's about it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, Ok. Did you find that they helped at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: A little bit yeah, but it would just kind of take the edge off of the pain for a little bit and it came back.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And what kind of pain is it that you're experiencing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, it's kind of a a sharp pain over on the like the right side of my chest like maybe belly area.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK um the right side of your chest and belly area. Yeah OK, so is that pain, is it, did it start around the same time as the cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I think it, it might have started a little bit after.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and is this a pain that you've ever had before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't had anything like this happen before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Is the pain primarily there when you cough or is it present at all times?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say more so when I cough or if I'm like taking a big breath. Um yeah, kind of after after I have a coughing episode I take a deep breath and I really will feel the pain then.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and and um, you said that it's a sharp pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, yeah, more of a sharp pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, and is it any worse when you're doing activity, like when you're up and walking around?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, don't notice it with any any activity.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, um an since uh, since this coughing and this this right sided pain that you're talking about began, have you noticed any fevers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think, yeah, I've been hot the last few days and I I checked my temperature earlier today and it was like 38.6 so that was one of the reasons why I wanted to come in actually.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, well I'm glad that I'm really glad that you came in because yeah, we really want to get this looked into. Have you been around anyone that's been sick recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, but I I do some volunteer work at one of the homeless shelters at a few times a week, so I am around a lot of people.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you traveled anywhere recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I've been at home. And and doing the volunteer work.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK um. OK, and can you just give me an idea of any? Do you have any chronic conditions that you see your family doctor for regularly or anything you take medication for?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um yeah, I have type 2 diabetes. And I I take Metformin. Um I think an SGLT 2 inhibitor and then I use insulin for that as well. And I have some, it has affected my kidneys as well. The diabetes I mean.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you have a history of high blood pressure?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you take medication for that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh yeah, I do. It starts with an "a" I think, amlodipine.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK OK and do you have any history of heart problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I know. No, I haven't really had any chest pain. On the left side anyway.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, So you said that you have had a cough for a really long time, a dryer cough then you're having sputum now. But is that something you've seen the doctor for?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh yeah, I think I was called like bronchitis in the past or something. Something like that. One of the doctors, my family doctor told me it was because I was a smoker.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So just to make sure I have your list of medications, you take amlodipine, insulin metformin, and an SG LT2 inhibitor? You think anything else?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, and then yeah, amlodipine, uh, yeah, I think that that that's everything. Oh a multivitamin too.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK cool. I just wanted to ask you a few questions questions about your lifestyle in general. Do you live here in town?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do. Yeah, I live with my wife and at a house nearby.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, cool and you mentioned that you're a smoker?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so I've smoked for the last 30 years or so. About a pack per day.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Do you use any other substance?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Ok. And do you have any family history of respiratory or heart problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, my dad actually had a heart attack. He was in his 70s. I think my mom had high blood pressure, but other than that, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um and do you have any allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think just environmental stuff, no medications. I am aware of.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK. Well thank you for sharing all of that with me. I'm going to go over it with the physician that I'm working with and will kind of come back and let you know about the next steps.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, thank you, that sounds good.
